remarks: No tracked port carries a weather or closure entry this run. Nothing in the set is suspended, and the one active cyclone in the basin stays about 900 km clear of the nearest of them.

Dujuan has strengthened from severe tropical storm to typhoon since the 17 September read, but it is a Japan story rather than a container-port one. It is passing Hachijojima and running north-northeast into open water off the Kanto coast; ferry services to the Izu islands and some Hachijojima flights are cancelled, and a cruise ship is being held in Tokyo. Its closest approach to any tracked port is 911 km at Busan, at the current analysis position, and the forecast track only widens that gap. No threat rows are written.

The queues at Shanghai, Ningbo and Yantian are no longer a weather event and are deliberately left out of the port list. Saudel and Krovanh dissipated in early September; what remains is backlog converging with the pre-Golden Week export rush. The congestion series speaks for that on its own.

Linerlytica has not published a new congestion snapshot since 13 September. The API still answers for later dates but returns the 13 September figures under them, so the stored history was left untouched this run rather than padded with repeats.
